question: The granite for Olympic curling stones comes from one tiny, uninhabited island, home mostly to seabirds. Which country does that island belong to?
source_excerpt: Kays of Scotland makes the Olympic curling stones from granite quarried on Ailsa Craig, an uninhabited island about 16 km off Scotland's southwest coast.

extra.why_interesting: Curling looks like a global Olympic sport played everywhere from Canada to Japan. Yet every Olympic stone traces back to one bare rock in the sea. Players can reason toward the answer from curling's well-known roots.
extra.verification_notes: Olympic curling stones are made by Kays from granite quarried on Ailsa Craig, an uninhabited Scottish island, and this still held for the 2026 Milano Cortina Games (https://www.teamgb.com/article/ailsa-craig-everything-you-need-to-know-about-where-olympic-curling-stones/5EFRzBr6xItMWCr2XRyaTS).

explanation: It's Ailsa Craig, off Scotland's west coast. Its granite is so dense and water-resistant that teams from Canada to Japan all slide pieces of the same Scottish rock.
